questions.question: ______ expenditure and ______ receipts are shown by the government budget.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Estimated; estimated.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The government budget shows estimated expenditures and estimated receipts.**
 
• **Estimated expenditure and actual receipts** would mean that the government has budgeted a certain amount of spending but has actually received a different amount of revenue.
 
• **Actual expenditure and estimated receipts** would mean that the government has spent a certain amount but expects to receive a different amount of revenue.
 
• **Actual expenditure and actual receipts **would mean that the government has spent a certain amount and has received the exact amount of revenue that was expected.
 
• It is important for the government to accurately estimate its expenditures and receipts in order to create a realistic budget and avoid** **overspending or underspending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Expenditure refers to the amount of money spent by the government on various expenses such as **salaries, infrastructure development, subsidies,** etc.
 
• Receipts refer to the amount of money collected by the government through various sources such as taxes, fines, fees, etc.
 
• **Estimated; actual** would indicate that the government's revenue collection strategy may be flawed or inefficient.
 
• **Actual; estimates** would indicate that the government's expenditure planning may be flawed or inefficient.
 
• **Actual; actual **would indicate that the government's budget planning and execution is accurate.

questions.question: What is the percentage share of agricultural workers in India as per Census 2011?

__
 
• **The percentage share of agricultural workers in India as per Census 2011 is 54.6%.**
 
• This means that out of the total workforce in India, only 54.6% were engaged in agricultural activities as per the 2011 Census.
 
• This is a significant drop from the previous Census in 2001, which recorded **60% **of the total workforce as agricultural workers.
 
• **The decline in the percentage share of agricultural workers in India can be attributed to various factors such as industrialization, urbanization, and the shift towards the service sector.**

• The decline in the percentage share of agricultural workers in India has led to concerns about the sustainability of the agricultural sector and the livelihoods of farmers.
 
• Agriculture accounted for **43.96 percent** of India's workforce in **2021.**
 
• **The remaining half was split nearly evenly between the two other sectors, industries and services.**

questions.question: Ramlal marks up his goods by 40% and gives a discount of 10%. What is his net profit percentage?

For successive percentage changes, use the net effect formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +40% and Discount (b) = −10%

Net Profit % = 40 − 10 + [40 × (−10)] ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 30 − 4 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Markup Percentage = 40%

Discount Percentage = 10%

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/648b541e29f9eb1e8917f94774372ff3c9a49a15fd6e46c915a4c6afa9608b03.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + (40% of 100) = 140

⇒ Discount given = 10% on MP = (10 ÷ 100) × 140 = 14

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 140 − 14 = 126

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 126 − 100 = 26

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

Discount Calculation

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
